description: Phi: a play head that walks along the channels of a polyphonic cable and sends out the value it is over

inputs.text: The channels the play head reads; they are the buffer the expanders work on
Moves the play head; it needs this even when the next input is patched
Jumps the play head to the start of the next channel; with nothing arriving before the step ends, the head stops short of the next value
Returns the play head to its starting position

outputs.text: Goes high as the play head enters a new step, for the fraction of the clock period set on the menu
The value under the play head, after every expander in the chain has had its turn

notes: nothing moves without a clock: the play head only advances on the clock input, whether or not the next input is patched
the buffer here holds voltages, so InX adds and OutX cuts values rather than combining gates
menu: Use Phasor as input — reads the clock input as a rising ramp giving the position directly instead of as a clock
Connect Begin and End — joins the end of the buffer back to its beginning
Negative 'next' pulse steps in reverse direction — makes a negative pulse at the next input step backwards
Remember speed after reset — keeps the play head's speed across a reset, so it starts at once instead of after two clock pulses
Gate Length — a slider setting the length of the step trigger as a fraction of the step duration
Add Expander — places a ReX, ModX, InX or GaitX expander on the correct side of this module

inputs.0:
continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads no channels.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the phasor or clock input.
inputs.3:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
